why: Both analyses land on the key's hedgehog (culture plus new minimill technology, lowest cost, profit per ton) and cover the same brutal facts, but Analysis 1 explicitly calls the company already great and frames its stop-doing list as temptations to refuse: no diversifying beyond steel or going overseas, no added layers or diluted bonuses, and no iron-carbide scale-up. Analysis 2 rates the company only 'arguably near-great' and leans toward intervention (exit fabrication lines within 12 months, overhaul the board) without stating the no-diversification and preserve-the-culture decisions in its stop-doing list.
